campus: Catania — Department of Physics and Astronomy 'Ettore Majorana' (DFA)
admission_type: Open access with verification of curricular requirements and personal preparation; the programme page describes a mandatory oral admission interview. Non-EU applicants residing abroad enter through a public selection call based on qualifications, with a possible online interview or test.
admission_route: Non-EU citizens residing abroad: non_eu_public_selection_call through the UNICT Student Portal. EU/equated citizens and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy for at least one year: eu_pre_evaluation_webform, followed by the applicable enrolment procedure.
citizenship_track: non_eu_resident_abroad / eu_and_equated / non_eu_resident_in_italy. EU-equated applicants include citizens of Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and San Marino, and non-EU citizens who have lived legally in Italy for at least one year.
academic_requirements: For the 2026/27 non-EU selection: a bachelor's or higher degree awarded abroad, of at least three years and giving access to master's study in the awarding country, obtained no more than six years before application; an adequate academic background in Physics and Mathematics including at least one introductory quantum mechanics course. The programme's standing admission page additionally specifies at least 27 CFU in Mathematics and at least 75 CFU in Physics, an equivalent/recognized bachelor's degree, and no outstanding educational debt.
eligible_bachelor_backgrounds: A bachelor's or higher degree with an adequate academic background in Physics and Mathematics; the 2026/27 call does not give a closed list of degree titles.
curricular_subject_prerequisites: Adequate preparation in Physics and Mathematics, including at least one introductory course in quantum mechanics. The programme page also states minimum credit requirements of 27 CFU in Mathematics and 75 CFU in Physics.
degree_recency_limit: The bachelor's or higher degree must have been obtained no more than six years before application.
undergraduate_in_progress_allowed: Yes. For the 2026/27 non-EU selection, final-year candidates may apply conditionally but must obtain the bachelor's degree by 31 July 2026.
professional_experience_alternative: No professional-experience substitute is stated for Physics in the 2026/27 call.
language_requirements: Good written and spoken English at CEFR B2 level or higher, including the ability to use scientific English. For the 2026/27 international selection, this must be demonstrated by an accepted test or an exemption document.

english_certificate_thresholds.cambridge_min: Cambridge ESOL First Certificate in English (FCE) or higher

english_certificate_exemptions: A declaration from the university that awarded the bachelor's or master's degree confirming that English was the official language of the programme, or a self-declaration of citizenship of an English-speaking country.
italian_language_requirement: Not required for admission to this English-taught master's programme.
application_deadline_eu: 30 June 2026 (the 2026/27 pre-evaluation form for EU/equated applicants was open from 8 April 2026).
application_deadline_non_eu: 17 March 2026 at 23:59 GMT+1 (applications opened 10 February 2026 at 12:00 GMT+1). Successful visa applicants also had to submit Universitaly pre-enrolment by 31 July 2026.
results_publication_date: By 6 May 2026 for the non-EU public selection.
required_documents: Non-EU public selection: passport personal-data pages; bachelor's degree or enrolment certificate stating the expected graduation date; official translation into Italian or English where necessary; transcript listing examinations, grades, grading range and preferably GPA; official syllabi for all completed academic activities on university letterhead or bearing the university stamp; reference letter, preferably from a university professor; Europass-format CV in English; English-language certificate or exemption evidence; motivation letter in English (maximum 4,000 characters including spaces); signed summary sheet; and any additional supporting material. EU/equated pre-evaluation additionally lists the final secondary-school diploma, its Declaration of Value or comparability certificate, the bachelor's degree, Declaration of Value or comparability and verification for the bachelor's degree, transcript/Diploma Supplement, official syllabi, motivation letter, recommendation letter and English certificate.
entry_exam_or_test: The programme page describes an oral interview testing proficiency in the basic subjects required by the MSc. For the 2026/27 non-EU route, the committee scores qualifications out of 100: academic record up to 50 points, relevance of prior education up to 40, reference letter up to 5, and motivation up to 5; it may require an online interview or test. A score of at least 50/100 is suitable.
credential_recognition_documents: For foreign qualifications, official translations are required when documents are not in Italian or English. A Declaration of Value or ENIC/NARIC (CIMEA) Statement/Certificate of Comparability may support the application and is required at enrolment for non-EU visa applicants; EU/equated pre-evaluation explicitly requests comparability/Declaration of Value documentation for the secondary-school and bachelor's qualifications, plus verification of the bachelor's degree. Official syllabi must be on the foreign university's letterhead or bear its stamp.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.unict.it/it/corsi-numero-programmato/2026-2027/public-selection-admission-non-eu-students-living-abroad-english (the linked 2026/27 call states a total non-EU-abroad enrolment charge of EUR 306: EUR 140 regional tax, EUR 16 stamp duty and EUR 150 annual comprehensive contribution).
application_fee: EUR 10 per programme application for the 2026/27 non-EU public selection; non-refundable status is not explicitly stated on the call page.
enrolment_confirmation_fee: EUR 75, non-refundable, payable within 15 days of admission notification (the published timeline gives 21 May 2026 as the general deadline). It is credited toward the EUR 150 annual comprehensive contribution.
places_quota_non_eu: [uncertain] Not stated in the 2026/27 call table; the official table's 'available places' cell for Physics is blank.
places_quota_total: [uncertain] No total capacity is published in the 2026/27 call. The programme admission page says enrolment has no prescribed maximum.

source_quotes.quote: complete the online application form between 10th February 2026 12.00 (GMT +1) and 17th March 2026, 23.59 (GMT +1)
A bachelor’s or higher degree awarded abroad obtained since no more than six years
at least 27 CFU in the general area (ssd) of Mathematics

uncertainty_notes: The 2026/27 call annex for non-EU applicants specifies an adequate Physics/Mathematics background including introductory quantum mechanics, but does not repeat the programme page's numeric minimums of 27 Mathematics CFU and 75 Physics CFU. The programme page is not labelled by academic year and may represent the standing Italian/EU admission rules. Its statement that every applicant takes an oral interview also differs from the 2026/27 non-EU call, where an online interview/test is optional at the committee's discretion. No 2026/27 seat quota is published for Physics. The tuition figure reported is specific to non-EU students residing abroad; the standard EU/Italian contribution schedule may differ.
